description: Redesign the member invite flow — lightweight Invite model, server-side invite creation/claiming, restyled Members list, simplified bookie invite sheet, and 3-path player claim flow with deep linking

userStories.title: Create Invite SwiftData model
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a lightweight Invite model in SwiftData to track invite lifecycle without creating premature player records.
acceptanceCriteria: New `Invite` SwiftData `@Model` in `Booki/Models/Invite.swift` with fields: `id` (UUID), `bookieId` (UUID), `inviteCode` (String, 8-char), `email` (String?, optional), `createdAt` (Date), `expiresAt` (Date), `claimedAt` (Date?), `claimedByPlayerId` (UUID?), `needsSync` (Bool, default false), `version` (Int, default 0)
Add computed properties: `isExpired` (Bool, checks expiresAt < Date()), `isPending` (Bool, claimedAt == nil && !isExpired)
Add `Invite.self` to the ModelContainer schema array in the app entry point (BookiApp.swift or similar)
Explicit `init()` provided (private stored properties make synthesized init private)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: SwiftData schema change — requires deleting app from Simulator

userStories.title: Create Supabase invites table migration
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the invites table in Supabase so invite records can be stored server-side.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration SQL file in `supabase/migrations/` creating `invites` table with columns: `id` (uuid PK default gen_random_uuid()), `bookie_id` (uuid NOT NULL references bookies(id)), `invite_code` (text UNIQUE NOT NULL), `email` (text), `created_at` (timestamptz default now()), `expires_at` (timestamptz NOT NULL), `claimed_at` (timestamptz), `claimed_by_player_id` (uuid references players(id)), `version` (int default 0)
RLS enabled: bookie can SELECT own invites (bookie_id = get_user_bookie_id()), bookie can INSERT own invites
Service role can UPDATE (for claim_invite edge function)
Index on `invite_code` for fast lookups
Migration file documented in SUPABASE_MIGRATIONS.md
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Run with: npx supabase db push --project-ref vstfauqufwpdytmvjyfz

userStories.title: Create create_invite edge function
userStories.description: As a bookie, I want invite creation to be server-authoritative so codes are unique and secure.
acceptanceCriteria: New edge function at `supabase/functions/create_invite/index.ts`
Request body: `{ email?: string }` (email is optional)
Validates JWT in code — caller must be a bookie (query bookies table for auth user id)
Generates unique 8-char invite code (charset: A-Z, 2-9, excluding 0/O/1/I/L) with collision retry
Sets `expires_at` to 24 hours from now
Inserts invite record into `invites` table with `bookie_id` from authenticated user
Returns `{ success: true, invite_id, invite_code, invite_url: 'booki://invite/{code}', expires_at }`
Uses shared helpers: `_shared/cors.ts`, `_shared/supabase.ts`, `_shared/idempotency.ts`, `_shared/audit.ts`
Idempotency key support matching existing edge function patterns
Emits audit event on successful creation
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Deploy: npx supabase functions deploy create_invite --no-verify-jwt --project-ref vstfauqufwpdytmvjyfz

userStories.title: Create claim_invite edge function
userStories.description: As a player, I need a server-authoritative way to claim an invite that creates my player record and links me to the bookie.
acceptanceCriteria: New edge function at `supabase/functions/claim_invite/index.ts`
Request body: `{ invite_code: string, auth_user_id: string }`
Validates invite code exists in `invites` table, is not expired (`expires_at > now()`), and is not already claimed (`claimed_at IS NULL`)
Verifies auth user exists via `supabase.auth.admin.getUserById()`

Checks auth user is not already linked to any bookie: query `players` table for `auth_user_id` WHERE `claimed_at IS NOT NULL` — if found, return 409 `{ error: 'already_in_group', message: "You're already a member of another organizer's group." }`
Creates new Player record in `players` table: `name` = email prefix (before @), `status` = 'active', `auth_user_id`, `bookie_id` from invite record, `claimed_at` = now(), `credit_limit` = 10000
Updates invite record: `claimed_at` = now(), `claimed_by_player_id` = new player ID
Auto-confirms email on auth user via `admin.updateUserById(auth_user_id, { email_confirm: true })`
Returns `{ success: true, player_id, bookie_id, player_name }`
Uses shared helpers for CORS, Supabase client, idempotency, audit
Emits audit event on successful claim
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Uses service role client to bypass RLS (same pattern as claim_player). Deploy: npx supabase functions deploy claim_invite --no-verify-jwt --project-ref vstfauqufwpdytmvjyfz

userStories.title: Add invite sync to SyncService
userStories.description: As a developer, I need invites to sync from Supabase so the bookie sees pending invites locally.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `Invite` to `SyncService` download cycle alongside existing models
Fetch invites where `bookie_id` matches current bookie ID (same pattern as players sync)
Upsert downloaded invites into local SwiftData context (match on `id`)
Claimed invites update locally showing `claimedAt` and `claimedByPlayerId`
Expired invites are retained locally (UI filters them, not deleted from DB)
Uses same version/conflict resolution pattern as other models

userStories.notes: Follow existing SyncService patterns for Player/Bet/LedgerEntry downloads

userStories.title: Add Pending Invites section to Members list
userStories.description: As a bookie, I want to see outstanding invites above the member list so I know who hasn't joined yet.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `@Query private var invites: [Invite]` to PlayersListView
Compute `pendingInvites` = invites where `claimedAt == nil` (includes expired for display)
'PENDING INVITES' section header (Theme.caption, Theme.textSecondary, tracking 1.0) appears above member rows only if `pendingInvites` is non-empty
Each pending invite row shows: email if provided or 'Link invite' as label, invite code in monospaced font (Theme.bodyFont), expiration countdown ('Expires in Xh Ym' or 'Expired' in Theme.danger)
Muted visual treatment: `Theme.elevatedBackground` background (not `Theme.cardBackground`), `Theme.textSecondary` text
Expired invites show 'Expired' label in `Theme.danger`
Swipe-to-delete gesture on pending invite rows that deletes the invite from local context + marks for sync
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use TimeInterval math for countdown: (expiresAt.timeIntervalSince(Date())) / 3600 for hours, remainder for minutes

userStories.title: Invite Member sheet — Generate Link section

After generation: displays invite code (large, 28pt monospaced font), 'Expires in 24 hours' subtitle (Theme.textSecondary)
Copy button: copies `booki://invite/{code}` to `UIPasteboard.general.string` with haptic feedback (UIImpactFeedbackGenerator)
Share button: uses SwiftUI `ShareLink` or presents `UIActivityViewController` with the invite URL string
Sheet has a 'Done' button to dismiss
Loading state while edge function call is in-flight
Error state if edge function fails (inline alert)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use EdgeFunctionService for the API call. The invite URL format is booki://invite/{code}

userStories.title: Invite Member sheet — Email option

If `MFMailComposeViewController.canSendMail()` is false: copy link to clipboard + show alert 'Link copied! Mail is not configured — share the link manually.'

userStories.title: Register booki:// URL scheme for deep linking
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the app to handle booki://invite/{code} URLs so invite links open directly in the app.
acceptanceCriteria: Register `booki` URL scheme in Info.plist under CFBundleURLTypes → CFBundleURLSchemes
Add `.onOpenURL` modifier on root view in app entry point (BookiApp.swift or ContentView.swift)
Parse invite code from URL: check scheme is 'booki', host is 'invite', extract first path component as code
Store parsed invite code in a published/state property that triggers navigation to InviteClaimView
If app is not authenticated: show InviteClaimView directly with the code
If app is authenticated as a bookie: show alert 'Switch to a member account to accept invites'
If app is authenticated as a player: route to InviteClaimView existing-user path
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: URL format: booki://invite/{CODE}. Use URLComponents to parse.

userStories.title: Invite claim landing screen
userStories.description: As an invited user, I want to see who invited me and have clear options to join.
acceptanceCriteria: New `InviteClaimView.swift` in `Booki/Views/`
Accepts optional `initialCode: String?` parameter (from deep link) or allows manual code entry
Manual code entry: text field with 8-char limit, auto-uppercase, filters non-alphanumeric (same pattern as existing PlayerClaimView)
On code submit/deep link: validates code against Supabase `invites` table (query where invite_code matches, not expired, not claimed) — fetches bookie name via bookie_id join
Valid code shows: Booki logo (BookiLogo image), 'You've been invited to join **[Bookie Name]**'s group' text, two CTAs
Primary CTA: 'Get Started' button (Theme.accent background, full-width)
Secondary CTA: 'Already have an account?' text link (Theme.accent foreground)
Invalid/expired code: error state 'This invite has expired or is invalid' in Theme.danger
Styled with Theme.background, centered content layout matching existing auth screens
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Reference existing PlayerClaimView for code entry formatting patterns and Supabase validation approach

userStories.title: Invite claim — new user signup path
userStories.description: As a new user accepting an invite, I want to create an account and join the bookie's group.
acceptanceCriteria: 'Get Started' from InviteClaimView navigates to account creation screen within same view (step-based navigation)
Account creation screen: email field + password field (min 6 chars) + confirm password field, dark themed matching existing auth screens
On submit: calls `supabase.auth.signUp(email: email, password: password)`
On signup success: calls `claim_invite` edge function via EdgeFunctionService with invite_code + auth_user_id from signup response
On claim success: triggers agreement acceptance flow (existing `submitPlayerAgreement()` / AgreementService pattern)
After agreement: calls `completePlayerClaimFlow` pattern — signs in fresh, app routes to player main view via AuthManager
Error handling: duplicate email, weak password, network failure — shown as inline error text below form (Theme.danger)
Loading state on submit button while API calls are in-flight
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Follow existing PlayerClaimView step 2 pattern for signup + claim sequence. Use AuthManager for session management.

userStories.title: Invite claim — existing user login path
userStories.description: As an existing user, I want to log in and join a bookie's group using my invite.
acceptanceCriteria: 'Already have an account?' from InviteClaimView navigates to login screen (email + password fields, dark themed)
On successful login via `supabase.auth.signIn(email:password:)`: calls `claim_invite` edge function
If claim succeeds (user has no existing bookie): shows confirmation screen 'Join [Bookie Name]'s group?' with Confirm and Cancel buttons
On Confirm: claim is already done, route to player main view via AuthManager
If claim returns 409 `already_in_group`: shows error screen 'You're already a member of another organizer's group. You cannot join multiple groups.' with a 'Back' button that returns to landing
Cancel button returns to InviteClaimView landing
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The 409 error case is the key differentiator from the new user path. claim_invite handles the check server-side.
